title: Structural Modeling Identifies a Conserved ADAR1 dsRBDIII Motif Predicted to Interact with PKR at Thr451
abstract:
Protein kinase R (PKR) is a key cellular dsRNA sensor whose activation is regulated by ADAR1. Although ADAR1–PKR association is established, its molecular determinants remain poorly understood. Molecular docking identified a conserved W768/F769/P770 (WFP) motif within ADAR1 dsRBD III as a potential PKR-interaction interface. Disruption of this motif altered the predicted binding configuration. However, co-immunoprecipitation revealed no significant reduction in PKR association following individual substitutions or deletion of the WFP motif, although the deletion showed a consistent trend toward reduced binding. RNase treatment reduced PKR co-immunoprecipitation approximately tenfold without abolishing the interaction. These findings suggest that ADAR1–PKR association is predominantly RNA-dependent, potentially involving shared dsRNA substrates that facilitate direct protein–protein contacts, with the WFP motif contributing to interaction stability.

Abstract Figure

Graphical Abstract:

Schematic representation of ADAR1p150 and PKR domain organization, predicted ADAR1– PKR interaction interface, and experimental validation.

(Top left) Domain organization of adenosine deaminase acting on RNA 1 p150 (ADAR1p150), showing the N-terminal Z-DNA-binding domains (Zα and Zβ), three double-stranded RNA-binding domains (RI, RII, and RIII), and the C-terminal deaminase domain (DD). The W768/F769/P770 motif (WFP motif) is highlighted in RIII. (Top right) Domain organization of protein kinase R (PKR), showing its two N- terminal double-stranded RNA-binding motifs (RI and RII) and C-terminal kinase domain (KD). The adjacent structural representation highlights the PKR kinase domain and the region containing Thr451 (T451), a residue implicated in PKR activation. (Bottom left) Predicted ADAR1–PKR interaction interface generated by protein–protein docking. ADAR1 RBDIII is shown in green, and the PKR kinase domain is shown in cyan and magenta to distinguish the displayed protein regions or chains. The ADAR1 residues Trp768 (W768), Phe769 (F769), and Pro770 (P770) are highlighted near PKR Thr451, illustrating their proximity within the predicted interface. The RNA strand shown beneath the complex illustrates the context of double-stranded RNA recognition and is not necessarily part of the docked protein–protein complex. (Bottom right) In-vitro co-immunoprecipitation (Co-IP) analysis comparing PKR association with wild-type ADAR1p150 (ADAR1-GFP WT) and the combined WFP mutant (WFP). The bar graph shows the relative PKR signal recovered in ADAR1 immunoprecipitates; error bars indicate variability between measurements, and ns denotes a statistically non-significant difference between the groups.
